CALGARY, Alberta, Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Enerflex Ltd. (TSX: EFX) (NYSE: EFXT) (“Enerflex” or the “Company”) today announced the appointment of Christine Morris as Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, effective January 1, 2027. Ms. Morris will succeed Preet S. Dhindsa, who will step down from his role effective December 31, 2026.

Paul Mahoney, Enerflex’s President and Chief Executive Officer, commented: “We thank Preet for his leadership and contributions to Enerflex over the past three years. During his tenure as CFO and period as interim CEO, Enerflex successfully completed the integration of Exterran, strengthened its financial flexibility, and established a solid foundation for continued growth and shareholder value creation.”

Mr. Mahoney continued, “We are pleased to welcome Christine to Enerflex at a critical point for the Company. As we progress towards the strategic objectives highlighted during our May investor update, our priorities remain clear. We are focused on capturing end market opportunities that can drive meaningful growth across the business, improving profitability, enhancing cash conversion, and driving higher returns on capital. Christine’s deep financial and leadership experience are highly complementary to our leadership team, and we look forward to her strong contributions as Enerflex drives value creation through growth and direct shareholder returns.”

About Christine Morris
Ms. Morris is a seasoned public company CFO and strategic advisor with a global track record of driving shareholder value. She has over 30 years of global financial leadership experience across the energy, industrial, and technology sectors, holding senior roles with major international organizations, including BT Group, Maersk Drilling, BJ Services, and Halliburton. Ms. Morris’ expertise spans financial strategy, operational performance, capital markets, mergers and acquisitions, and business transformation.

Ms. Morris holds a Master of Business Administration from Stanford University, a Master of Science in Actuarial Sciences, and a Bachelor of Science in Mathematical Sciences from the Catholic University of Louvain in Belgium.

ABOUT ENERFLEX
Enerflex is a leading provider of modular natural gas, power, and treated water technology solutions, delivering value through disciplined execution and a deliberate approach to where we compete. Our customer-focused delivery model supports operational excellence, innovation, and scalability across our global footprint with a focus on creating long-term shareholder value.

With approximately 4,500 engineers, manufacturers, technicians, professionals, and innovators, Enerflex is bound together by a shared vision: Transforming Energy for a Sustainable Future. The Company remains committed to the future of natural gas and the critical role it plays, while focused on sustainability offerings to support the world’s energy needs.

Enerflex’s common shares trade on the Toronto Stock Exchange under the symbol “EFX” and on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol “EFXT”. For more information about Enerflex, visit www.enerflex.com.

SINGAPORE, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- JOYY Inc. (NASDAQ: JOYY) (“JOYY” or the “Company”), a global technology company, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter of 2026.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights1

  • Net revenues were US$624.6 million, an increase of 15.6% from US$540.2 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and an increase of 5.7% from US$590.8 million in the second quarter of 2026.
    • Social Entertainment net revenues increased by 8.8% to US$441.0 million from US$405.5 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and by 4.3% from US$422.7 million in the second quarter of 2026.
    • BIGO Ads net revenues increased by 39.6% to US$145.7 million from US$104.4 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and by 9.0% from US$133.7 million in the second quarter of 2026.
    • Shopline net revenues increased by 24.7% to US$37.8 million from US$30.3 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and by 10.0% from US$34.4 million in the second quarter of 2026.
  • Operating income was US$13.5 million, compared with US$19.6 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$13.8 million in the second quarter of 2026.
  • Non-GAAP EBITDA2 was US$55.7 million, an increase of 10.1% from US$50.6 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and compared with US$56.9 million in the second quarter of 2026.
  • Net income from continuing operations attributable to controlling interest of JOYY3 was US$59.6 million, compared with US$62.0 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$51.8 million in the second quarter of 2026.
  • Non-GAAP net income from continuing operations attributable to controlling interest and common shareholders of JOYY4 was US$67.1 million, compared with US$72.4 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$63.5 million in the second quarter of 2026.
  • Net Cash5 as of September 30, 2026 was US$2,940.5 million.
  • Net Cash from operating activities was US$102.2 million, compared with US$73.4 million in the corresponding period of 2025.

Third Quarter 2026 Business Highlights

Global community:

  • Global average mobile MAUs6 reached 278.8 million in the third quarter of 2026, up by 4.7% from 266.2 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and up by 0.6% from 277.1 million in the second quarter of 2026. The Company continued to optimize its marketing strategies to focus on return on investment (ROI) and high-value users.

Social Entertainment:

  • In the third quarter, Social Entertainment revenues increased by 8.8% year over year to US$441.0 million, with live streaming revenues reaching US$419.8 million, an 8.1% increase from the corresponding period of 2025. By region, live streaming revenues showed year-over-year growth across all four geographical areas.
  • In the third quarter, core live streaming paying users7 increased by 8.1% year over year to 1.64 million, while ARPPU8 was US$218.7.
  • Bigo Live continued to make enhancements across content operations, streamer ecosystem, and AI-driven capabilities. In content operations, the Company refined its cross-regional content algorithms, expanded live translation coverage and noise-resilient speech recognition, enabling users to discover diverse content and interact with streamers across regions. Improved onboarding and guidance for newly signed streamers contributed to a 4.7-percentage-point sequential increase in the share of newly signed streamers completing their first livestream. The Company also continued to expand AI-generated interactive content and virtual gifts. In September 2026, AI-generated interactive virtual gifts accounted for 35.4% of total virtual gift consumption on Bigo Live.

B2B Initiatives: Advertising Technology and Smart Commerce

  • Beginning in 2022, the Company ramped up efforts to diversify its revenue streams, cultivating its new initiatives in advertising technology and smart commerce. The Company has made steady progress advancing towards its strategic positioning as a global tech company powered by multiple growth engines. In the third quarter, total non-live streaming revenues reached US$204.7 million, up by 34.9% year over year, representing 32.8% of total net revenues of the Company, compared with 28.1% in the corresponding period of 2025.

BIGO Ads:

  • BIGO Ads is a global AI-powered programmatic advertising platform. Launched to provide one-stop marketing and monetization solutions, it leverages deep learning, real-time bidding, and smart bidding models to enable brands to scale user acquisition and app developers to effectively unlock monetization potential through connecting premium global demand.
  • In the third quarter, BIGO Ads’ total revenues grew by 39.6% year over year to US$145.7 million. In particular, BIGO Audience Network, which includes third-party advertising revenues generated on network partners’ traffic properties, maintained robust growth, with revenues increasing by 52.3% year over year.
  • BIGO Ads has access to a vast traffic pool, comprising the Company’s own global average mobile MAU base and an extensive network of third-party traffic through seamless integration of developer traffic across major channels. During the third quarter, Software Development Kit (SDK) traffic scale continued to expand, increasing by 55.6% year over year.
  • Broader traffic coverage, multi-vertical advertiser expansion, and ongoing algorithm optimization continued to fuel growth. Web-based demand grew approximately 328% year over year and 30% quarter over quarter, alongside solid performance from in-app demand.
  • BIGO Ads continued to invest in its algorithm and engineering infrastructure during the quarter. As its cross-channel attribution systems improved and advertiser conversion data accumulated, BIGO Ads broadened its data inputs for model training, improving predictions of conversion probability and user lifetime value. The platform also upgraded its model architecture to support different conversion objectives and traffic types, while refining its bidding algorithm to better assess the value of each ad impression and allocate advertiser budgets more effectively.

Shopline:

  • Shopline serves as a global AI-powered operating system for modern retail. Beyond storefront creation, Shopline offers a deeply integrated suite of merchant services across payments, logistics, marketing, and data analytics. It is an open, extensible omnichannel platform that enables merchants to manage the full commerce value chain from store setup and transactions to fulfillment, customer acquisition, and lifecycle engagement. Shopline has helped merchants in diverse industries across multiple markets to launch and scale their businesses.
  • Shopline currently generates revenues from recurring software subscription fees and a suite of transaction-based value-added services, including localized payment processing (Shopline Payments) and marketing solutions.
  • In the third quarter, Shopline generated revenues of US$37.8 million, up 24.7% year over year and 10.0% quarter over quarter. Notably, cross-border merchants revenue increased by 77.8% year over year. The Company continued to enhance Shopline Payments with more local payment options, stronger multi-currency payment support, and improved transaction management, helping merchants manage cross-border payments more easily and efficiently.
  • As AI platforms and agents emerge as new channels for product discovery and purchasing, Shopline continued to strengthen its AI Commerce capabilities. On the ecosystem front, Shopline expanded its integrations with leading AI platforms and AI agents, and enhanced its AI tools and interfaces for developers. On the merchant operations front, the Company rolled out its AI-powered commerce assistant, Shopline Omi, spanning product management, customer segmentation, promotional events, multilingual support, and detailed store performance analysis.

Ms. Ting Li, Chairperson and Chief Executive Officer of JOYY, commented, “This quarter, we made further progress toward becoming a global technology company powered by multiple growth engines. Total net revenues reached US$624.6 million, up 15.6% year over year and 5.7% quarter over quarter. Our Social Entertainment business remained on a steady course, while BIGO Ads and Shopline sustained robust performances, driving solid topline expansion and strong operating cash flow generation. We remain steadfast in our commitment to shareholder returns, having returned a total of US$536.0 million year-to-date through November 13, 2026, comprising US$216.2 million in dividends and US$319.8 million in share repurchases.

Social Entertainment revenues grew 8.8% year over year to US$441.0 million, supported by continued enhancements to Bigo Live’s content operations, streamer ecosystem, and AI-driven capabilities. Live streaming revenues and core live streaming paying users both increased 8.1% year over year. BIGO Ads revenues rose 39.6% year over year to US$145.7 million, led by 52.3% year-over-year growth in BIGO Audience Network as we expanded our traffic network, diversified advertiser demand, and improved our algorithms and ad delivery. Shopline revenues reached US$37.8 million, up 24.7% year over year, supported by continued expansion among cross-border merchants and strong momentum in Shopline Payments. We also advanced our AI Commerce initiatives to help merchants reach customers through emerging AI-powered shopping channels and strengthen Shopline’s role as an omnichannel e-commerce infrastructure platform.

Looking ahead to 2027, we believe JOYY will enter a pivotal phase in which our established strategy translates into stronger operating results. With clearer strategic trajectories across our three businesses, we are well positioned to deliver diversified and sustainable growth while creating long-term shareholder value.”

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

NET REVENUES

Net revenues were US$624.6 million, representing an increase of 15.6% from US$540.2 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and an increase of 5.7% from US$590.8 million in the second quarter of 2026.

Social Entertainment net revenues increased by 8.8% to US$441.0 million from US$405.5 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and by 4.3% from US$422.7 million in the second quarter of 2026. The year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter increases were primarily driven by higher live streaming revenues, as expanded content categories and enhanced localized operations contributed to stronger user engagement and paying conversion across key markets.

BIGO Ads net revenues increased by 39.6% to US$145.7 million from US$104.4 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and by 9.0% from US$133.7 million in the second quarter of 2026. The year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter increases were primarily driven by expansion of traffic, elevated advertiser demand across regions and verticals, and enhanced algorithm performance that resulted in improved advertisement delivery efficiency and higher advertiser spending.

Shopline net revenues increased by 24.7% to US$37.8 million from US$30.3 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and by 10.0% from US$34.4 million in the second quarter of 2026. The year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter increases were primarily driven by continued merchant adoption and deeper penetration of value-added services.

COST OF REVENUES AND GROSS PROFIT

Cost of revenues was US$407.4 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with US$347.1 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$389.2 million in the second quarter of 2026.

Social Entertainment’s cost of revenues increased by 7.4% year over year to US$274.3 million, and by 3.7% from US$264.6 million in the second quarter of 2026. The year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter increases were primarily attributable to higher revenue-sharing fees and content costs of US$28.4 million and US$7.9 million, respectively.

BIGO Ads’ cost of revenues increased by 47.9% year over year to US$112.2 million, and by 5.6% from US$106.3 million in the second quarter of 2026. The year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter increases were primarily attributable to higher traffic acquisition costs paid to third-party partners in relation to the expansion of BIGO Audience Network.

Shopline’s cost of revenues increased by 30.8% year over year to US$20.9 million, and by 13.9% from US$18.3 million in the second quarter of 2026. The year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter increases were primarily attributable to higher payment processing costs, reflecting an increased contribution from payment services to Shopline’s revenue mix.

Gross profit was US$217.2 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with US$193.1 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$201.6 million in the second quarter of 2026. Gross margin was 34.8% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with 35.8% in the corresponding period of 2025 and 34.1% in the second quarter of 2026.

OPERATING EXPENSES AND INCOME

Operating expenses were US$204.1 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with US$174.2 million in the same period of 2025 and US$188.2 million in the second quarter of 2026. Among the operating expenses, sales and marketing expenses were US$86.7 million, compared with US$72.1 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$79.6 million in the second quarter of 2026. Research and development expenses were US$59.0 million, compared with US$63.1 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$53.0 million in the second quarter of 2026. General and administrative expenses were US$58.4 million, compared with US$39.1 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$55.6 million in the second quarter of 2026.

Operating income was US$13.5 million, compared with US$19.6 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$13.8 million in the second quarter of 2026.

Non-GAAP operating income9 was US$46.6 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with US$40.7 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$49.1 million in the second quarter of 2026. Non-GAAP operating income margin10 was 7.5% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with 7.5% in the corresponding period of 2025 and 8.3% in the second quarter of 2026.

Non-GAAP EBITDA was US$55.7 million, compared with US$50.6 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$56.9 million in the second quarter of 2026. Non-GAAP EBITDA margin11 was 8.9%, compared with 9.4% in the corresponding period of 2025 and 9.6% in the second quarter of 2026.

NET INCOME

Net income from continuing operations attributable to controlling interest of JOYY was US$59.6 million, compared with US$62.0 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$51.8 million in the second quarter of 2026. Net income margin was 9.5% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with 11.5% in the corresponding period of 2025 and 8.8% in the second quarter of 2026.

Non-GAAP net income from continuing operations attributable to controlling interest and common shareholders of JOYY was US$67.1 million, compared with US$72.4 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$63.5 million in the second quarter of 2026. Non-GAAP net income margin12 was 10.7% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with 13.4% in the corresponding period of 2025 and 10.7% in the second quarter of 2026.

NET INCOME PER ADS

Diluted net income from continuing operations per ADS13 was US$1.20 in the third quarter of 2026, compared with US$1.15 in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$1.01 in the second quarter of 2026.

Non-GAAP diluted net income from continuing operations per ADS14 was US$1.36 in the third quarter of 2026, compared with US$1.36 in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$1.24 in the second quarter of 2026.

BALANCE SHEET AND CASH FLOWS

As of September 30, 2026, the Company had net cash of US$2,940.5 million, compared with US$3,258.0 million as of December 31, 2025. For the third quarter of 2026, net cash from operating activities was US$102.2 million.

SHARES OUTSTANDING

As of September 30, 2026, the Company had a total of 952.0 million common shares outstanding, representing the equivalent of 47.6 million ADSs assuming the conversion of all common shares into ADSs.

Business Outlook

For the fourth quarter of 2026, the Company expects net revenues to be between US$650 million and US$669 million. This forecast reflects the Company’s current and preliminary views on the market, operational conditions, and business strategies, which are subject to change, particularly as to the potential impact from macroeconomic uncertainties.

Share Repurchase Programs

Pursuant to the Company’s up-to-US$600 million share repurchase program authorized in May 2026, or the 2026 Share Repurchase Program, which is effective through the end of 2028, the Company had repurchased approximately 1.6 million ADSs for an aggregate consideration of US$120.5 million on the open market during the third quarter of 2026.

Between October 1, 2026 and November 13, 2026, the Company repurchased an additional approximately 0.5 million ADSs, for an aggregate consideration of US$38.4 million under the 2026 Share Repurchase Program. The remaining unutilized amount under the 2026 Share Repurchase Program was approximately US$368.2 million as of November 13, 2026.

Quarterly Dividend Program

On May 22, 2026, the board of directors of the Company authorized a quarterly dividend program, or the 2026 Dividend Program, under which a total of approximately US$900 million in cash will be distributed on a quarterly basis between 2026 and 2028.

Pursuant to the 2026 Dividend Program, the board of directors has accordingly declared a dividend of US$1.59 per ADS, or US$0.0795 per common share, for the third quarter of 2026, which is expected to be paid on January 15, 2027 to shareholders of record as of the close of business on December 30, 2026. The ex-dividend date will be December 30, 2026.

Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures

The unaudited condensed consolidated financial information is prepared in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (“U.S. GAAP”). Non-GAAP net income (loss) from continuing operations attributable to controlling interest and common shareholders of JOYY is net income (loss) from continuing operations attributable to common shareholders of JOYY excluding share-based compensation expenses, impairment of goodwill and investments, amortization of intangible assets from business acquisitions, gain (loss) on deconsolidation and disposal of subsidiaries and business, gain (loss) on disposal and deemed disposal of investments, gain (loss) on fair value change of investments, reconciling items on the share of equity method investments, interest expenses related to the convertible bonds’ amortization to face value, accretion, cumulative dividend and deemed dividend to subsidiaries’ preferred shareholders, gain on repurchase of redeemable convertible preferred shares of a subsidiary and income tax effects of above non-GAAP reconciling items and adjustments for non-GAAP reconciling items for the net income (loss) from continuing operations attributable to non-controlling interest shareholders. 6 Refers to average mobile monthly active users of the social entertainment platforms operated by the Company, including Bigo Live, Likee, imo and Hago. Average mobile MAU for any period is calculated by dividing (i) the sum of the Company’s active mobile users for each month of such period, by (ii) the number of months in such period.

7 Core live streaming paying users during a given period is calculated as the cumulative number of registered user accounts that have purchased virtual items or other products and services on Bigo Live, Likee or imo at least once during the relevant period.

Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - Emerita Resources Corp. (TSXV: EMO) (OTCQX: EMOTF) (FSE: LLJA) (the "Company" or "Emerita") announces that it has posted a presentation on its website providing additional information on the Pre-Feasibility Study ("PFS") for its wholly-owned Iberian Belt West Project ("IBW") in Spain.

The presentation provides an overview of the PFS results announced on October 29, 2026, including the technical and financial considerations of IBW, and addresses certain questions raised by shareholders following the release of the PFS.

"We appreciate our shareholders' patience while we prepared the presentation. It provides a more detailed overview of the technical and financial aspects of IBW and addresses many of the questions we have received following the release of the PFS results. We will continue to provide shareholders with updates as work on IBW progresses," commented Joaquin Merino, President and Chief Executive Officer of Emerita.

The presentation is available on the Company's website at www.emeritaresources.com.

VALLEY FORGE, Pa.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--UGI Corporation (NYSE: UGI) today reported financial results for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2026 and provided guidance for fiscal year 2027.

HEADLINES

  • GAAP net income of $692 million and adjusted net income of $665 million compared to GAAP net income of $678 million and adjusted net income of $728 million in the prior year.
  • GAAP diluted earnings per share (“EPS”) of $3.12 and adjusted diluted EPS of $3.00 compared to GAAP diluted EPS of $3.09 and adjusted diluted EPS of $3.32 in the prior year.
  • Delivered adjusted diluted EPS that exceeded our revised guidance range issued on May 6, 2026, inclusive of approximately $0.10 cents of incremental tax benefits associated with the renewable natural gas facilities previously placed in service.
  • Achieved growth in reportable segments earnings before interest expense and income tax1 ("EBIT") of $1,198 million, when compared to $1,176 million in the prior year.
  • Strengthened the balance sheet with available liquidity of approximately $1.8 billion and a leverage ratio of 3.8x at UGI Corporation.
  • Invested approximately $900 million of capital, with 77% directed to our natural gas businesses, including completing the replacement of cast iron main at UGI Utilities nearly a year ahead of our February 2027 commitment.
  • Advanced portfolio optimization through divestiture of the LPG operations in seven countries and the pending sale of the PA Electric Utility for approximately $470 million, subject to customary closing conditions.
  • Subsequent to year-end, successfully concluded the gas base rate case at:
    • UGI Utilities, which comprised a two-phase, $65 million distribution rate increase ($40 million effective October 2026; $25 million effective October 2027) with a stay-out provision until January 2029.
    • Mountaineer Gas, a net revenue increase of $17 million effective December 1, 2026, with a stay-out provision until February 2028.
  • Issues Fiscal 2027 adjusted diluted EPS guidance range of $2.90 - $3.202.

Updated data from a more mature October 2026 data cutoff show rapid and deep responses, with a 39% confirmed ORR, median duration of response of 9.2 months and median PFS of 6.7 months

Clinical activity consistent across HPV status and prior-treatment subgroups, with a manageable safety profile

Results support advancement of MICVO into the global Phase 3 HeadlinerSM trial in 2L+ R/M HNSCC, planned to initiate in mid-2027

Company to host a live webcast on November 19, 2026, at 7:00 a.m. EST, following the late-breaking oral presentation

BOSTON, Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Pyxis Oncology, Inc. (Nasdaq: PYXS), a clinical-stage company developing next-generation therapeutics for difficult-to-treat cancers, today announced updated results from its ongoing global Phase 1 monotherapy study evaluating micvotabart pelidotin (MICVO) in patients with second-line and beyond recurrent/metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (2L+ R/M HNSCC).

The results will be presented on November 19, 2026, by Faye Johnson, M.D., Ph.D., professor of thoracic/head and neck medical oncology at The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center, in a late-breaking oral presentation at the 38th EORTC-NCI-AACR Symposium on Molecular Targets and Cancer Therapeutics in Barcelona, Spain.

The updated data, as of October 14, 2026, demonstrated a 39% confirmed objective response rate (cORR), 94% disease control rate (DCR), median progression-free survival (mPFS) of 6.7 months, 12-month overall survival (OS) probability of 81%, and newly reported median duration of response (mDOR) of 9.2 months among 33 efficacy evaluable patients dosed at 5.4 mg/kg intravenously once every three weeks with a dose equivalent to or below a dose cap. Together, these results provide further evidence of clinical activity across HPV statuses and prior-treatment subgroups, with an expected and manageable tolerability profile.

“We are grateful to the EORTC-NCI-AACR Symposium for highlighting these updated MICVO data in 2L+ R/M HNSCC, and to Dr. Johnson for presenting these important new results,” said Tom Civik, Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of Pyxis Oncology. “The data from October show improvements across multiple key clinical activity endpoints with a novel analysis showing that MICVO increased mPFS by 50% versus the most recent prior therapy patients had received before MICVO. We are also very happy to report that our clinical strategy for managing safety has had the intended impact. There have been no new cases of Grade 3 peripheral neuropathy and the six patients that experienced Grade 3 peripheral neuropathy have all improved with five of the six patients resolving to Grade 1 or better. Collectively, this updated data profile, and the new analyses further support our plan to advance MICVO into the global Phase 3 HeadlinerSM trial in 2L+ R/M HNSCC, which we expect to initiate in mid-2027. With important regulatory meetings in the near term and more mature overall survival (OS) data expected in the first half of 2027, we remain confident in our path forward.”

“For patients whose disease progresses after platinum chemotherapy and immunotherapy, there remains a substantial unmet medical need, particularly as we anticipate broader use of EGFR-targeted therapies in earlier lines of treatment,” said Dr. Johnson. “It is reassuring to see responses that last in this setting and, if confirmed in a larger study, MICVO could potentially offer these patients a meaningful new treatment option.”

Planned Separation Intended to Unlock Long-Term Shareholder Value and Create Two Companies, Each a Leader in Its Respective Industry With Tailored Capital Allocation Priorities, Attractive Dividend Yield, and Meaningful Growth Opportunities

Enhances Strategic and Financial Flexibility for Each Company

Establishes UGI Corporation as a Premier Natural Gas Infrastructure Company Operating in Favorable U.S. Load-Growth Markets and Low-Cost Supply Regions

New Global LPG Company Expected To Be The Largest Publicly Listed LPG Distribution Company in The World Following The Separation

UGI Corporation to Host Conference Call and Webcast on Thursday, November 19, 2026, at 8:00 AM ET

VALLEY FORGE, Pa.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--UGI Corporation (NYSE: UGI) today announced that its Board of Directors unanimously approved a plan to pursue the separation of its Global LPG business (the new LPG Company) from UGI to create two publicly traded companies, each well-capitalized with tailored capital allocation strategies and strongly positioned to serve customers, pursue strategic growth objectives and create significant, long-term shareholder value. UGI intends to execute the separation through a spinoff of the new LPG Company that is expected to be tax-free to UGI and its shareholders for U.S. federal income tax purposes. The spinoff is expected to be completed during the second half of calendar year 2027.

“The creation of the new LPG Company is the next step in our company’s transformation, building on the portfolio optimization, balance sheet strengthening, and operational improvements we have achieved. The separation positions both companies for long-term growth, strategic optionality, and significant value creation for shareholders and customers,” said President and Chief Executive Officer, Robert Flexon. “Each company will have distinct strategies and operating priorities with capital allocation and supporting resources directed to its greatest opportunities for success and market leadership.”

Flexon continued, “We move forward with great confidence in the future of both companies and their respective abilities to serve customers and communities with excellence.”

Anticipated Benefits of the Planned Separation

As separate companies, the New UGI and the new LPG Company are expected to benefit from:

  • Sharper strategic alignment: Focused management and business models aligned with each company’s markets, customers, and capital needs;
  • Tailored capital structures: Balance sheets and capital return policies aligned to each company’s financial profile and cost of capital;
  • Capital and strategic flexibility: Investments aligned with each company’s growth opportunities and other long-term shareholder value-creating alternatives; and
  • Distinct investment profiles: Discrete business models allowing investors to assess each company based on its operational and financial characteristics.

New UGI: A Premier Natural Gas Infrastructure Company in the Mid-Atlantic Region

Following the completion of the separation, the New UGI will be a premier natural gas infrastructure company with fully regulated natural gas utilities and complementary midstream assets located in a favorable long-term supply basin, with direct access to low-cost Marcellus and Utica supply, and ideally positioned to serve customers demanding safe, reliable, and affordable natural gas in the Mid-Atlantic region. Demand megatrends for natural gas, including the need for generation to support the power grid, data center development, and rising industrial activity, are expected to further drive sustainable growth for the New UGI. Its operations will include:

  • UGI Utilities, Inc.: Operates the second largest regulated natural gas utility in Pennsylvania, serving approximately 700,000 customers across 46 counties;
  • Mountaineer Gas Company: The largest regulated natural gas utility in West Virginia, serving more than 209,000 customers across 55 counties; and
  • UGI Energy Services, LLC: Includes natural gas pipeline and gathering assets with a total capacity of 5.1 MMDth/day and storage facilities with approximately 15 Bcf of capacity, as well as LNG peaking assets.

The New UGI is expected to benefit from consistent earnings growth and solid, recurring cash flows backed by a constructive regulatory framework that allows over 90% recoverability of capital spend within 12 months, a $5 billion regulated rate base expected to grow 8 – 10% per year, and fee-based contract structures covering more than 80% of midstream margins. Approximately 90% of the New UGI’s margins are de-risked through its regulated utility operations, take-or-pay and minimum volume commitments, and fixed-fee arrangements. Cash flows for the New UGI are expected to be directed to capital investments that promote safe, reliable, affordable, and sustainable energy; targeted system expansion opportunities; maintaining a strong balance sheet and investment-grade credit profile; and an attractive dividend for shareholders.

As a regulated utility and in keeping with UGI’s current focus on affordability and service excellence, the separation transaction should not have an impact on customers or customer rates.

New LPG Company: The Largest Publicly Traded LPG Distribution Company in the World Following the Separation

The new standalone LPG Company is expected to be a scaled leader in Europe and the largest retail propane distributor in the United States. The new LPG Company’s assets meet critical energy needs in the regions it serves and are strategically located near diverse supply channels, providing a competitive advantage that has resulted in a broad and diverse customer base spanning the residential, commercial, industrial, and agricultural sectors. With resilient unit margins, a targeted EBITDA margin of 17 – 20%, and expected growth in free cash flow, the new LPG Company will be well positioned to deliver a compelling and growing dividend, combined with share repurchases, while investing in targeted growth opportunities. Its operations will include:

  • UGI International: A leading distributor of LPG in nine countries in western and northern Europe and the largest in France, Belgium, Denmark, Luxembourg and Finland; and
  • AmeriGas Propane, Inc.: Serves approximately 950,000 customers in 49 states from approximately 1,300 distribution locations and a network of more than 41,700 cylinder-exchange outlets.

Contract structures and hedging programs within the new LPG Company will continue to support strong cash flow generation. UGI International has a track record of solid operational execution, and AmeriGas Propane has made meaningful progress on its operating improvement and safety initiatives while strengthening its balance sheet, leaving the business better positioned for volumetric growth. Building on these efforts will be a priority for the new LPG Company as it enters its next phase of growth.

Following the separation, cash flows for the new LPG Company, are expected to be directed to a compelling and growing dividend, share repurchases, and targeted strategic growth investments, while maintaining a strong balance sheet and industry-leading credit profile.

Separation Transaction Details

Under the proposed spinoff plan, UGI’s shareholders will retain their current shares of UGI common stock and receive a pro-rata distribution of shares of the new LPG Company’s stock in a transaction that is intended to be tax-free to UGI and its shareholders for U.S. federal income tax purposes. After the completion of the spinoff, the New UGI may retain a stake of up to 19.9% in the new LPG Company, which would be exited in a tax-efficient manner over time.

The spinoff transaction is subject to final approval from the UGI Board of Directors, the effectiveness of a registration statement on Form 10 to be filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission, and satisfaction of other customary conditions, including receipt of required consents, waivers or amendments under our and our subsidiaries’ debt agreements, or repayment under or termination of such agreements. There can be no assurance that any separation transaction will ultimately occur or, if one does occur, its structure, terms, timing, or tax treatment.

UGI intends to continue its quarterly dividend, subject to approval by its Board of Directors, with a payout ratio in line with peers, building on its 142 consecutive years of dividend payments.

Further details regarding the proposed capital structure, capital allocation strategy, dividend policy, governance, and leadership team for each company will be defined as part of the separation planning and communicated at a later date.

Conference Call and Webcast

UGI will hold a live audio webcast of its conference call to discuss this announcement and its fiscal 2026 financial results at 8:00 AM ET on Thursday, November 19, 2026.

Interested parties may listen to the webcast both live and in replay on the Internet at https://www.ugicorp.com/investors/financial-reports/events-and-presentations or by visiting the UGI website at https://www.ugicorp.com and clicking on “Investors” and then “Events and Presentations.”

Advisors

J.P. Morgan Securities LLC is serving as lead financial advisor to UGI, and Latham & Watkins LLP is serving as legal advisor.

About UGI

UGI Corporation (NYSE: UGI) is a distributor and marketer of energy products and services in the U.S. and Europe. UGI offers safe, reliable, affordable, and sustainable energy solutions to customers through its subsidiaries, which provide natural gas transmission and distribution, electric generation and distribution, midstream services, propane distribution, renewable natural gas generation, distribution and marketing, and energy marketing services.

Comprehensive information about UGI Corporation is available on the Internet at https://www.ugicorp.com.

Use of Non-GAAP Measures

Management uses free cash flow (“FCF”) and EBITDA margin, each a non-GAAP financial measure, to evaluate the new LPG Company’s cash generation and operating performance. Management believes these measures provide investors with useful supplemental information about the new LPG Company’s historical cash generation and expected performance, including its capacity to fund dividends, share repurchases and growth investments.

  • We define FCF as cash from operating activities and proceeds from the sale of assets in the normal course of business, less capital expenditures.
  • We define EBITDA margin as adjusted EBITDA divided by revenue.

These non-GAAP measures are not calculated in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”) and should be considered in addition to, and not as a substitute for, the most directly comparable GAAP measures.

Targets for EBITDA margin and expected growth in FCF are forward-looking non-GAAP measures. Key Terms

spinofffinancial
A spinoff is when a company separates part of its business into a new, independent company and gives existing shareholders shares in that new business. For investors, it matters because the move can clarify what each business is worth, let the separate companies focus on their own goals, and change risk and return — similar to converting one mixed-use property into two specialized apartments that may attract different buyers and rents.
ebitda marginfinancial
EBITDA margin is the share of each dollar of sales that a company keeps as operating cash profit before interest, taxes, and accounting for equipment wear and long-term investments. Think of it like the cash a store has left from every sale after paying day-to-day running costs but before paying rent, loan interest or replacing old machinery. Investors use it to compare core profitability and operational efficiency across companies by removing financing and accounting differences.
non-gaapfinancial
Non-GAAP refers to financial measures that companies use to show their earnings or performance without including certain expenses or income that are often added back to give a different picture. It matters because it can make a company's results look better or more favorable, but it may also hide important costs, so investors need to look at both GAAP (official rules) and non-GAAP numbers to get a full understanding.
View in glossary
form 10regulatory
Form 10 is a U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission filing companies use to register their securities and become subject to public reporting requirements, delivering a comprehensive package of business descriptions, audited financial statements, management information and risk factors. For investors it matters because it creates a standardized, permanent dossier on a company—like a full inspection and disclosure packet when buying a house—so you can assess finances, risks and management and compare firms reliably.

Under the Arrangement, QeM will acquire all of the issued and outstanding Plurilock Shares. Shareholders will receive C$0.084 in cash and 0.0763 of a common share of QeM (each whole common share of QeM, a "QeM Share") in exchange for each Plurilock Share they hold (together, the "Consideration"), implying total consideration of C$0.28 per Plurilock Share. All outstanding restricted share units will vest immediately prior to the effective time of the Arrangement and be settled for the Consideration. All outstanding warrants and convertible debentures of Plurilock will, in accordance with their terms and without further action by the holders thereof, entitle the holders to receive, upon exercise or conversion, the Consideration in lieu of Plurilock Shares.

  • Poster presented today at CTOS 2026 expands on the survival data first reported in the abstract (announced 11 November 2026), which showed a 12-month disease-free survival (DFS) of 81.1% in patients with resectable soft tissue sarcoma.
  • Patients with post-treatment tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) levels above 310 cells/mm² had 95.0% 12-month DFS compared with 64.9% in patients with lower TIL levels.
  • Patients with treatment-related hyalinisation and fibrosis greater than 52% had 93.8% 12-month DFS compared with 71.4% in patients with lower levels.
  • Results build on previously reported strong pathological responses and further support the potential of efti-based combination therapy.

SYDNEY, AUSTRALIA, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Immutep Limited (ASX: IMM; NASDAQ: IMMP) (“Immutep” or the “Company”), a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing novel LAG-3 immunotherapies for cancer and autoimmune diseases, today announced new data from the investigator-initiated EFTISARC-NEO Phase II study presented at the Connective Tissue Oncology Society (CTOS) 2026 Annual Meeting (Poster number P 448).

The study is evaluating Immutep’s eftilagimod alfa (efti) in combination with KEYTRUDA® (pembrolizumab) and radiotherapy before surgery in patients with high-risk, resectable soft tissue sarcoma. Forty patients were enrolled, and 38 patients underwent surgery and were included in the survival evaluation.

The latest analysis currently shows a disease-free survival (DFS) of 81.1% at 12 months. The current Kaplan-Meier estimate at 18 months is also 81.1%, although this later time point remains immature, and follow-up is ongoing. Among the 38 patients who underwent surgery and were evaluated, eight patients had experienced disease recurrence at the data cut-off (April 30, 2026).

Table 1 – Survival results for soft tissue sarcoma patients from EFTISARC-NEO

OutcomeLatest Analysis
12-month disease-free survival (mature)81.1%
18-month disease-free survival (immature)81.1%
12-month local recurrence-free survival94.1%
12-month distant metastasis-free survival86.2%
Median follow-up19.1 months


In addition, exploratory analyses showed that higher levels of tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) and greater hyalinisation and fibrosis after treatment may be associated with better DFS. In particular, patients with post-treatment TIL levels above 310 cells/mm² had 95.0% 12-month DFS compared with 64.9% in patients with lower TIL levels. Patients with treatment-related hyalinisation and fibrosis greater than 52% had 93.8% 12-month DFS compared with 71.4% in patients with lower levels of hyalinisation and fibrosis. The presence of tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) and baseline expression of PD-L1, LAG-3 and TIGIT did not correlate with survival outcomes.

These survival and exploratory findings build on previously reported EFTISARC-NEO results in which the trial met its primary endpoint with a median tumour hyalinisation/fibrosis of 51.5% following neoadjuvant therapy with efti, pembrolizumab and radiotherapy. The new data are consistent with efti's mechanism of action, in which activation of antigen-presenting cells drives a stronger anti-tumour T cell response, and suggest that a stronger immune response in the tumour may be associated with improved patient survival outcomes.

Pawel Sobczuk, MD PhD, one of the Principal Investigators of EFTISARC-NEO, said: “These results are highly encouraging for patients with high-risk soft tissue sarcoma, where recurrence remains a major concern despite surgery and radiotherapy. Disease-free survival of approximately 81% maintained through 12 months and on a preliminary basis also at 18 months is an important observation, and the association between a strong immune response in the tumour and better disease-free survival is particularly compelling. Together with the substantial pathological responses previously reported, the findings reinforce the potential of this novel neoadjuvant approach and provide a strong rationale for continued follow-up and further clinical evaluation.”

Marc Voigt, CEO of Immutep, said: “With the data to date, EFTISARC-NEO is delivering an increasingly coherent and encouraging picture. The marked difference in outcomes between patients with higher and lower post-treatment immune cell infiltration is especially notable and is consistent with efti’s potential to help generate a stronger anti-tumour immune response. We believe these results strengthen the rationale for further potential clinical development in this indication, where patients remain in need of more effective treatment options.”

The poster is available on the Posters & Publications page of Immutep’s website.

Next Steps

Immutep anticipates reporting additional data from EFTISARC-NEO in CY2027.

Subject to regulatory interactions, manufacturing timelines, partnering arrangements and available resources, the Company is preparing to advance efti into a registration-directed clinical trial in neoadjuvant soft tissue sarcoma, targeting initiation in H2 CY2027.

About EFTISARC-NEO

EFTISARC-NEO is an investigator-initiated, open-label Phase II trial evaluating eftilagimod alfa (efti) in combination with KEYTRUDA® (pembrolizumab) and radiotherapy as neoadjuvant treatment for patients with resectable soft tissue sarcoma. The trial is led by the Maria Skłodowska-Curie National Research Institute of Oncology in Warsaw, Poland, and is primarily funded by a grant from the Polish Medical Research Agency, with Immutep supplying efti.

The primary endpoint is pathological response, measured as the percentage of tumour hyalinisation/fibrosis at resection. Secondary endpoints include safety, disease-free survival, local recurrence-free survival, distant metastasis-free survival, overall survival, radiological response and health-related quality of life. Forty patients were enrolled, with enrolment completed in January 2025 (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06128863).

About Eftilagimod Alfa (efti)

Eftilagimod alfa (efti) is Immutep’s proprietary soluble LAG-3 protein and MHC Class II agonist that activates antigen-presenting cells through the MHC Class II pathway, engaging both innate and adaptive immunity, including the priming of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells and the production of co-stimulatory signals and cytokines. Its favourable safety profile enables combination with anti-PD-(L)1 therapy, radiotherapy and/or chemotherapy. Efti has received Fast Track designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in first-line head and neck squamous cell carcinoma and first-line non-small cell lung cancer, and Orphan Drug Designation in soft tissue sarcoma.

About Immutep

Immutep is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing novel immunotherapies for cancer and autoimmune disease. The Company is a pioneer in the understanding and advancement of therapeutics related to Lymphocyte Activation Gene-3 (LAG-3), and its diversified product portfolio harnesses LAG-3’s ability to stimulate or suppress the immune response. Immutep is dedicated to leveraging its expertise to bring innovative treatment options to patients in need and to maximise value for shareholders. For more information, please visit www.immutep.com.

CHEYENNE, Wyo.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Payward, Inc., an integrated financial services and market infrastructure platform, today announced it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Tribe Capital Management, Inc., a venture capital and asset-management platform that uses AI and data science to underwrite and deploy capital across early- and late-stage private investments.

Customers increasingly demand access to early-stage companies, private-market opportunities, and emerging AI and technology investments. Tribe Capital’s capabilities across these segments will become a key part of Payward’s Asset Management pillar.

Tribe Capital brings investment sourcing, underwriting, portfolio construction, and fund-management capabilities that complement Payward’s existing infrastructure. They will expand the range of investment products available across Payward’s consumer, professional, and institutional client base.

“Joining Payward gives us the opportunity to bring Tribe’s investment approach to a global financial platform,” said Jonathan Hsu, co-founder of Tribe Capital. “We see a strong fit between our investment approach and Payward’s infrastructure, distribution, and product-building capabilities.”

Payward plans to build on Tribe Capital’s existing investment platform to develop new private-market offerings that draw on its infrastructure and distribution. The combination will connect investment origination and asset management with capabilities across custody, trading, collateral, and tokenization. Tribe Capital is expected to operate within Payward’s Asset Management pillar, alongside Trading, Banking, Services, and AI.

Tribe Capital, which has $2.7 billion in assets under management, invests across early- and late-stage private companies through commingled funds and co-investment vehicles. It was founded in 2018 on the premise that investment decisions in startups could be faster and better by paying close attention to operating and product-engagement data. Its portfolio spans companies applying AI and advanced software across technology and financial infrastructure.

The transaction is subject to customary closing conditions, including required consents, and is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027. Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed.

Key Terms

assets under managementfinancial
Assets under management (AUM) is the total value of all the investments that a financial company or fund is responsible for overseeing on behalf of its clients. It’s like a big bucket that shows how much money the firm is managing for people or organizations. A higher AUM often indicates a larger, more trusted company, and it can influence how much money they earn and the services they can offer.
commingled fundsfinancial
An investment vehicle that pools money from multiple investors into a single portfolio managed together; each investor owns a pro rata interest rather than specific, separately held securities. Commingled funds are often structured as trusts or partnership vehicles and are used by institutions and pooled accounts (for example retirement plan collective trusts), with the manager making buying and selling decisions for the combined pool; they can differ from mutual funds and ETFs in regulatory oversight, reporting, investor eligibility, and liquidity or redemption terms.
co-investment vehiclesfinancial
A co-investment vehicle is a fund-like arrangement that lets outside investors put money directly into a specific deal alongside a lead investor, rather than investing in the lead investor’s larger fund. Think of it like joining a neighbor to buy a single rental property instead of buying into their whole portfolio: it can cut fees and boost potential returns but concentrates risk and often has less liquidity, so investors need to weigh higher upside against greater exposure to one investment.
